key_insight: Spindle current signal coherence can reveal groove defect formation in friction stir welding before the defect becomes visibly apparent.
engineering_relevance: This enables low-cost, sensor-light real-time monitoring of FSW on standard CNC machining centers for earlier quality control and process intervention.
method: Segment spindle and axis current signals from defect-free and defected FSW runs
Extract FFT, PSD, and spectral coherence features
Compare signal changes against XCT for transient groove formation
evidence_signal: The study found that defective regions showed a marked drop in coherence at the spindle fundamental frequency and harmonics, with process instabilities detected about 10 s after defect initiation and confirmed by XCT.
watch_item: Performance may depend on machine-specific current signatures, so calibration and validation are needed before deployment across different CNC/FSW setups.
paper_title: Early detection of groove defect in friction stir welding through data-driven process monitoring
